title: Late-Time Observations of Type Ia Supernova SN 2014J with the Hubble Space Telescope Wide Field Camera 3
extended_summary:
This paper is an astrophysics observational study of late-time photometry of Type Ia supernova SN 2014J, not an education or AI-in-education intervention study. The author presents complementary Hubble Space Telescope Wide Field Camera 3 observations of SN 2014J taken roughly 365 to 1296 days after B-band maximum light, focusing on the late-time light curves in the F438W, F555W, and F814W filters.

The main analytical goals are to determine whether the measured photometry is contaminated by unresolved light echoes and to test whether the late-time decline rates of SN 2014J are consistent with previously reported correlations between supernova luminosity and late-time light-curve flattening. The author compares SN 2014J colors to those of SN 2011fe to rule out unresolved echo contamination, and directly compares F438W and F555W decline rates for several supernovae (SN 2011fe, 2012cg, 2014J, 2015F, and ASASSN-14lp) to avoid pseudo-bolometric reconstruction assumptions.

The study concludes that SN 2014J’s photometry is not contaminated by an unresolved light echo and that the late-time decline-rate pattern remains consistent with the earlier claim that more intrinsically luminous SNe Ia have flatter, slower-declining late-time light curves. The paper emphasizes that the main remaining limitation is the small supernova sample size, which prevents a definitive test of the correlation.
